description: Knowledge of internal statistical holdings, administrative data sources, external data providers, and reusable analytical assets across the organization.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
change to work: This activity would shift from mainly creating or adapting databases for specific requests toward first identifying whether suitable existing datasets, linked assets, or reusable statistical products already exist. Database development would increasingly be positioned as reuse optimization, integration, or enhancement of existing assets rather than a default response to new user demand.
justification: The current wording emphasizes developing databases for requests, but the update requires a prior discovery step across existing holdings and external sources before development begins.

description: Ability to navigate catalogues, metadata repositories, registries, and documentation systems to locate and assess fit-for-purpose data assets.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
change to work: This activity would shift from mainly creating or adapting databases for specific requests toward first identifying whether suitable existing datasets, linked assets, or reusable statistical products already exist. Database development would increasingly be positioned as reuse optimization, integration, or enhancement of existing assets rather than a default response to new user demand.
justification: To determine whether new development is needed, the role must be able to search, compare, and interpret metadata-rich assets in digital environments.

description: Ability to assess whether existing datasets, time series, linked records, or prior outputs can satisfy user needs with minimal new development.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
change to work: This activity would shift from mainly creating or adapting databases for specific requests toward first identifying whether suitable existing datasets, linked assets, or reusable statistical products already exist. Database development would increasingly be positioned as reuse optimization, integration, or enhancement of existing assets rather than a default response to new user demand.
justification: The future expectation explicitly prioritizes reuse and solution-oriented thinking over creating new collection vehicles or bespoke assets.

description: Ability to explain and defend complex cost-benefit, timeliness, burden, and risk-based recommendations to clients and governance stakeholders.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
change to work: Consultation will become more challenging and advisory in nature. Instead of mainly helping users obtain requested outputs, the specialist will need to challenge assumptions about data needs, explain why reuse or alternative sources may be preferable, and justify when new collection is not warranted. Advice will include feasibility, burden, timeliness, automation, and governance implications.
justification: The updated role requires communicating not just data possibilities but evidence-based decisions on why a request should be met through reuse or denied as a new collection.

description: Understanding of how automation, machine-assisted processes, and AI-enabled methods affect feasibility, efficiency, data sourcing, and option selection.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
change to work: Consultation will become more challenging and advisory in nature. Instead of mainly helping users obtain requested outputs, the specialist will need to challenge assumptions about data needs, explain why reuse or alternative sources may be preferable, and justify when new collection is not warranted. Advice will include feasibility, burden, timeliness, automation, and governance implications.
justification: The specialist must now bring automation and AI considerations into early consultation, which is not explicit in the current role profile.

description: Ability to prepare and present comparative options, including reuse, administrative data, linkage, or new collection, with documented rationale.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Represents subject matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles.'
change to work: Representation on committees and projects would increasingly involve advocating for reuse-first approaches, documenting needs assessments, and bringing evidence on feasibility, digital integration, and data asset options into governance and decision forums.
justification: Committee participation will now require stronger governance-oriented analysis and structured justification for new or avoided collection activity.

description: Ability to evaluate and document comparative costs, operational feasibility, timeliness, respondent burden, privacy, and quality risks across sourcing options.
historic work: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.'
change to work: This is the most directly affected element. The activity would be updated to require a formal sequence: identify the need, scan existing data assets, assess alternative sources, compare solution options, evaluate burden/risk/timeliness/cost, and document the rationale for any recommendation. 'Special studies' would no longer be the implicit default; instead, the role would need to prove that no suitable existing solution is available before initiating new collection or bespoke production.
justification: The update explicitly requires documented cost-benefit, timeliness, and risk assessments before new collection is initiated.

justification: The future role requires more formal and traceable decision-making than the current text implies.

justification: The update expects the role to challenge default assumptions and validate whether a new survey is actually required.

description: Knowledge of strengths, limitations, access conditions, coverage, comparability, and risks of non-survey data sources.

Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.'

'Special studies' would no longer be the implicit default; instead, the role would need to prove that no suitable existing solution is available before initiating new collection or bespoke production.
justification: Selecting among internal, administrative, and external sources requires stronger knowledge breadth than a narrower source-identification approach.

description: Ability to scope projects based on comparative sourcing options, reuse potential, and organizational capacity constraints.
historic work: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.'
change to work: Project definition will become more gated and conditional. Before work plans are finalized, the specialist will need to document why the need cannot be met through existing assets and assess downstream effects on organizational resources, digital integration, and operational burden. Projects may be less 'unique' and more explicitly assessed for alignment with reusable platforms and standard approaches.
justification: The update requires evidence-based prioritization tied to reuse, automation, and resourcing implications rather than only bespoke project planning.

description: Knowledge of how early source-selection decisions affect design, collection, processing, dissemination, evaluation, and governance.
historic work: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.'
change to work: Project definition will become more gated and conditional. Before work plans are finalized, the specialist will need to document why the need cannot be met through existing assets and assess downstream effects on organizational resources, digital integration, and operational burden. Projects may be less 'unique' and more explicitly assessed for alignment with reusable platforms and standard approaches.
justification: Formalized front-end decisions now require stronger understanding of how early choices affect downstream phases and enterprise resources.

description: Ability to communicate the comparative suitability, constraints, and trade-offs of data-source options in non-technical and technical contexts.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communication - 'Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs.'
change to work: Advisory communication will expand to include data-source strategy, the merits and limitations of administrative and alternative data, and the rationale for not pursuing new collection unless clearly necessary. Guidance will increasingly include methodological implications of reuse and digital sourcing choices.
justification: The advisory role now includes defending source strategy and the consequences of reuse-first decisions to sophisticated audiences.

description: Ability to negotiate preferred solutions using documented comparative analysis of cost, timeliness, burden, quality, risk, and feasibility.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communication - 'Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.'
change to work: This element becomes more central because the future state requires formal option comparison and negotiation around whether new collection should occur at all. The specialist will need to argue for reuse, phased solutions, automation, or alternate sourcing based on documented evidence rather than only negotiating implementation details.
justification: The update explicitly emphasizes solution-oriented thinking and robust business cases for new surveys.

description: Knowledge of metadata standards, data cataloguing practices, lineage information, and discoverability mechanisms used to identify fit-for-purpose data assets.
historic work: Technical Activities - Knowledge of specialized fields - 'Knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.'
change to work: This knowledge requirement expands beyond manipulation, storage, and retrieval toward discovery, reuse assessment, metadata interpretation, and cross-source suitability analysis. The role will need deeper understanding of how data assets are catalogued, documented, linked, and assessed before use.
justification: Current knowledge focuses on handling statistical data once in use, but the update requires earlier-stage discovery and suitability assessment.

development area: Enterprise and external data ecosystem knowledge
description: Knowledge of organizational data inventories, administrative sources, external providers, access pathways, stewardship responsibilities, and source constraints.
historic work: Technical Activities - Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.'
change to work: This element broadens from knowledge of other programs to a stronger enterprise-wide awareness of data holdings and reusable assets across the organization and beyond. The updated role requires understanding who owns what data, how it can be accessed, what restrictions apply, and where alternative sources may substitute for collection.
justification: The future expectation explicitly requires proactive scanning of all existing data holdings and alternative data sources first.

development area: Front-end data governance and risk assessment
description: Knowledge of how privacy, confidentiality, security, quality, and respondent burden requirements apply when comparing existing and new data-source options.
historic work: Technical Activities - Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.'
change to work: This element will need to be applied earlier in the process during source selection and business-case development, not only during project conduct. Privacy, confidentiality, security, and quality implications of reusing administrative or external data must be considered during needs identification and option screening.
justification: The update requires early risk assessment before initiating collection or selecting alternatives, extending policy application into front-end decision-making.

description: Ability to compare data sources for conceptual fit, coverage, timeliness, quality, integration potential, and operational viability before initiating work.
historic work: Technical Activities - Research and analysis - 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses).'
change to work: The reference to integrating multiple sources becomes more foundational and moves earlier in the workflow. The role will need to analyze source comparability and fitness before project launch, rather than primarily during downstream processing design. This makes pre-project source assessment a stronger analytical responsibility.
justification: The current role mentions integrating sources, but the update requires assessing them earlier and more systematically as alternatives to new collection.

development area: Digital workflow, automation, and AI applicability
description: Knowledge of where automation and AI can support data discovery, source assessment, workflow efficiency, and reduction of unnecessary collection.
historic work: Technical Activities - Research and analysis - 'Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.'
change to work: This element expands to include assessing whether automation, digital workflows, or AI-enabled methods can reduce the need for new collection, improve reuse, or support more efficient needs fulfilment. Technology assessment becomes an earlier decision input rather than only a production-procedure concern.
justification: The future state explicitly mentions feasibility, automation, and AI considerations during early stakeholder engagement and solution selection.

description: Ability to convert user needs into documented options, recommendations, and defensible business cases.
historic work: Job Poster - Experience - 'Providing consultative services to internal or external users.'
change to work: The experience expectation should evolve from general consultation toward evidence-based advisory work that includes source-option analysis, challenge of collection requests, and formal recommendation writing.
justification: Future consultation is more governance-heavy and analytically structured than the generic consultative expectation currently stated.

development area: Pre-project appraisal and source strategy planning
description: Ability to conduct front-end planning that includes source discovery, feasibility review, and decision gates before formal project launch.
historic work: Job Poster - Experience - 'Planning and organizing statistical projects, work plans, production schedules, and dissemination activities.'
change to work: This experience requirement would need to include planning at the pre-project stage, especially evaluating whether a project should proceed at all, what source strategy is most appropriate, and whether a reusable or automated pathway exists.
justification: The update changes planning from implementation-focused scheduling to earlier options appraisal and go/no-go justification.

description: Ability to identify candidate data assets, evaluate fitness for purpose, and select among them before extraction or transformation work starts.
historic work: Job Poster - Skills - 'Data manipulation'
change to work: Data manipulation remains relevant but is no longer sufficient on its own. The future role requires stronger upstream capability in locating, understanding, and comparing candidate data assets before manipulation begins.
justification: Current skills emphasize handling data once obtained; the updated role requires stronger pre-acquisition discovery and assessment capability.

description: Ability to work across repositories, metadata systems, and catalogues to identify, access, and compare relevant data assets.
historic work: Job Poster - Skills - 'Database management'
change to work: Database management would increasingly include navigating enterprise data environments, understanding metadata structures, and identifying reusable assets rather than only managing specific operational databases.
justification: The future workflow is driven by discovery and reuse across holdings, not only management of known databases.

description: Knowledge of how administrative, existing program, external, and linked data can substitute for or complement surveys.
historic work: Job Poster - Domain Knowledge - 'Survey collection processes'
change to work: Survey process knowledge remains important, but it will need to be reframed as one option among several rather than the implicit baseline solution. The role must understand when survey collection is unnecessary or unjustified relative to administrative or existing data reuse.
justification: The update explicitly establishes new data collection as a last resort, creating a gap if the role is primarily grounded in survey-centric thinking.

development area: Digital data discovery and consultation platform proficiency
description: Ability to use enterprise data discovery platforms, metadata catalogues, search interfaces, and AI-assisted consultation tools to identify reusable data assets and support rapid client discussions.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
change to work: This activity will shift from broad consultative support oriented toward responding to requests and defining custom outputs to a more structured facilitation role using digital discovery environments. Consultative services will increasingly involve guiding users through available holdings, metadata, quality indicators, reuse options, and trade-offs rather than primarily eliciting requirements for new studies. The specialist will need to support real-time, evidence-based discussions using platform outputs and organizational prioritization criteria.
justification: Current wording emphasizes subject-matter expertise and consultation, but does not explicitly require digital discovery platform use, AI-supported consultation, or metadata-guided facilitation. The future consultation model depends on these capabilities.

description: Ability to lead structured discussions on fitness-for-use, quality, timeliness, cost, and reusability, and explain why some options are preferred or rejected.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
change to work: This activity will shift from broad consultative support oriented toward responding to requests and defining custom outputs to a more structured facilitation role using digital discovery environments. Consultative services will increasingly involve guiding users through available holdings, metadata, quality indicators, reuse options, and trade-offs rather than primarily eliciting requirements for new studies. The specialist will need to support real-time, evidence-based discussions using platform outputs and organizational prioritization criteria.
justification: The updated role requires the specialist to explain quality, timeliness, feasibility, and value trade-offs transparently during consultations, which is more explicit and structured than in the current description.

development area: Enterprise data holdings and metadata knowledge
description: Knowledge of available internal datasets, linked assets, administrative sources, historical series, metadata standards, and their reuse constraints to support needs assessment without defaulting to new collection.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
change to work: This activity will shift from broad consultative support oriented toward responding to requests and defining custom outputs to a more structured facilitation role using digital discovery environments. Consultative services will increasingly involve guiding users through available holdings, metadata, quality indicators, reuse options, and trade-offs rather than primarily eliciting requirements for new studies. The specialist will need to support real-time, evidence-based discussions using platform outputs and organizational prioritization criteria.
justification: The current work-description references knowledge of users and provision of advice, but not deep operational knowledge of discoverable enterprise holdings required to support first-use of existing assets.

description: Ability to evaluate whether existing datasets, time series, linked holdings, or standard products can satisfy user requirements before developing new data structures or bespoke outputs.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
change to work: This activity will be reframed away from frequent development of bespoke databases for special requests toward maximizing reuse of existing data assets, discoverable holdings, and reusable data products. New database or data product development will more often follow an explicit assessment showing that current assets cannot meet the need. The role therefore becomes more selective and justification-oriented in initiating custom outputs.
justification: The current activity assumes ongoing development for special studies and requests. The future state requires a stronger capability to assess reuse potential before building new products.

description: Knowledge of strategic prioritization frameworks, value-for-money principles, and business rules used to determine whether custom development or new collection is justified.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
change to work: This activity will be reframed away from frequent development of bespoke databases for special requests toward maximizing reuse of existing data assets, discoverable holdings, and reusable data products. New database or data product development will more often follow an explicit assessment showing that current assets cannot meet the need. The role therefore becomes more selective and justification-oriented in initiating custom outputs.
justification: The specialist will need to justify when new products are not warranted and when alternatives better align with organizational priorities.

description: Ability to use AI-supported discovery and decision-support tools to assess whether existing data assets can meet stated needs, including feasibility, timeliness, and quality implications.
historic work: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.'
change to work: This decision-making function is directly transformed. Investigation of requirements will now begin with a structured exploration of existing data holdings and alternative sources using automated discovery and metadata tools. Defining special studies will become a later-stage option rather than an initial response. The specialist will need to determine not only sources and methods, but also whether new work is warranted at all after documented feasibility and cost-benefit review. Decision-making will therefore become more comparative, transparent, and constrained by reuse-first principles.
justification: Current decision-making expects the specialist to define special studies and determine data sources, but not to conduct formal reuse-first digital triage supported by automated tools.
